verdict.rationale: Resend's own API-key creation supports least-privilege scoping: a `sending_access` permission limits a key to sending emails only, and that key can be further restricted to a single domain. Key rotation is also documented. The scoping is coarse, though: only a send-only tier with a domain restriction is evidenced, with no fine-grained per-resource or per-endpoint scopes, expiry or TTL, or agent-specific credential flow, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: fine-grained per-resource/per-endpoint scopes, key expiry/short-lived credentials, agent-specific credential issuance guidance, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Restrict an API key to send emails only from a specific domain. This is only used when the `permission` is set to `sending_access`.
Add a new API key to authenticate communications with Resend.
